title: War, peace and the death penalty
tagline: How the Church weighs just war and pacifism, why the Catechism changed on the death penalty in 2018, and what it says about torture and nuclear weapons.
whyItMatters: These are questions where Catholics of good will disagree about application, and where the Church's own teaching has developed. The course helps you tell the settled from the disputed.

mindset.tip: Many listeners have fought, lost someone to violence, or been a victim. Hear them out before arguing (Romans 12:15).
Say that the Church holds legitimate defence and also the dignity of every person, even the guilty (CCC 2263-2267).
Present both sides in their strongest form: the just war tradition, and Christian nonviolence. Pax Christi and Aquinas disagree in emphasis, not in the goal of peace.
Be honest that CCC 2267 changed in 2018 and that some Catholics ask how that fits with earlier teaching. The Vatican calls it a development.
On torture and nuclear weapons, quote the documents; the language is strong and needs no embellishment.

resources.title: Summa Theologiae II-II, Q. 40: War

resources.title: Evangelium Vitae
